implementation_constraints: Pure Python 3.8+ standard library only (json, re, shlex, sys); no third-party dependencies and no filesystem or network access.
Verdict is communicated exclusively via process exit code (0 allow / 2 block); stdout is never used for the verdict, and a block writes one short reason line to stderr.
Fail-closed everywhere: unreadable stdin, invalid JSON, a non-object payload, a missing/non-string tool_name, a non-object tool_input, and any unexpected internal exception all exit 2.
Marker detection is a case-insensitive substring test on the whole string; tool names are lowercased before family lookup.
Three-way dispatch on tool family: a name-based read-only allowlist always allows; a shell allowlist gets command-text analysis; everything else blocks when the marker appears anywhere in tool_input.

Shell analysis is default-deny per stage: the command line is split on pipes, sequencing operators and newlines with quote/escape awareness, and EVERY stage must be provably read-only or the call blocks.

A stage is proven read-only only if it has no unquoted redirection, no command substitution, its resolved argv0 basename is on a read-only command allowlist, and it carries no in-place/output-write flag (including --flag=value forms and bundled short flags).
git is on the read-only command list but narrowed by subcommand; git config with a value argument is treated as a write.
Unknown-tool argument scanning walks nested dicts, lists and strings iteratively, inspects dict keys as well as values, and treats a pathological/oversized structure as a block.
Deliberately no execution, symlink resolution, or script-content inspection.
Exactly one self-contained file at source/guard.py runnable as python guard.py.

unresolved_intent.decision: Named a fixed case-insensitive allowlist (read/readfile/view/cat, grep/search/glob/find, ls/list/listdir, notebookread, webfetch/websearch plus snake_case and underscore aliases) rather than inferring intent from the tool name.
unresolved_intent.rationale: SPEC says the guard 'recognises this family of read-only tools by name' but never enumerates the names, and host tool naming varies. An allowlist is the fail-closed reading: an unrecognised reader falls through to the conservative unknown-tool branch and blocks only if it actually names a golden — a false block on a reader, never a false allow on a writer.

unresolved_intent.decision: Treated bash/sh/shell/zsh/cmd/powershell/pwsh/run/exec/execute/terminal (case-insensitive) as the shell family that receives command-text analysis; everything else outside the read-only list falls to the marker-anywhere rule.
unresolved_intent.rationale: SPEC names only 'e.g. Bash'. Misclassifying a shell as 'other' is safe (marker anywhere blocks, which is stricter); misclassifying a writer as a shell would let the read-only-command proof open a door, so the shell list is kept small and explicit.

unresolved_intent.decision: Enumerated a closed allowlist of reader commands (cat/bat/head/tail/less/grep/rg/ls/find/fd/diff/wc/sort/cut/jq/sha256sum/echo/pwd/git...) and treated every unlisted command — including sed, awk, tee, cp, mv, rm, python — as a writer.
unresolved_intent.rationale: SPEC mandates 'treat the command as a WRITE unless every part of it is a recognised read-only operation' but gives no vocabulary. A closed allowlist is the only formulation where an unknown command blocks; a denylist of writers would allow anything not yet imagined, which is exactly the failure the fail-closed posture forbids.

unresolved_intent.decision: Included git in the reader allowlist but gated it on a read-only subcommand list, and additionally treated git config with a value argument as a write.
unresolved_intent.rationale: git is both the most common way to read a golden (git show/diff/log) and a way to rewrite one (git mv/checkout/restore/apply). Excluding git entirely would block legitimate golden reads (AC-GH-03); including it wholesale would allow git mv on goldens. Subcommand gating is the narrowest cut that satisfies both.

unresolved_intent.decision: Blocked on a fixed flag set (-i, --in-place, -w, --write, --fix, -o, --output/--out-file, -O, --save, --overwrite, --replace, -p), matched on exact tokens, on --flag=value heads, and on each character of bundled short flags such as -ni.
unresolved_intent.rationale: SPEC describes the flags semantically without listing them, and short-flag bundling means a literal token match alone would miss sed -ni. Expanding bundles risks false positives on readers that use -i as ignore-case (grep -i), which is an over-block: acceptable under 'when in doubt, block', and it only triggers when the command already names a golden.

unresolved_intent.ir_region: shell call whose command field is absent or unparsable
unresolved_intent.decision: When a shell tool's arguments contain no readable command string, allow only if the marker appears nowhere in the arguments; block if it does. Unbalanced quoting in a present command makes stage splitting return no stages, which fails the read-only proof and blocks.
unresolved_intent.rationale: SPEC's fail-closed rule targets calls that touch a golden; a shell call with no command field and no marker anywhere cannot name a golden by text, so blocking it would break unrelated tool use without protecting anything. The moment the marker appears, the unprovable call blocks.
